Google's subsequent 12-year evolution fully validated this judgment — ultimately 80% of developers voluntarily migrated to Cider V, not because of mandates, but because of its integration depth and superior experience. This paradox shows that in the developer tools space, forced standardization often backfires, while organic evolution achieves true widespread adoption.
1hd2qfd:180: Cider's core innovation is moving code indexing, semantic analysis, and language services entirely to the cloud backend. At Google's scale (multiple commits per second, billions of lines of code), the traditional local IDE assumption — that "source code, build metadata, indexing, and analysis all happen locally" — completely collapses. Cider's lightweight client launches extremely fast, with all the "magic" happening on servers that can index the entire codebase in real time. This architectural choice gives it a decisive edge over traditional IDEs in fast-iteration scenarios.
